This bill abolishes the Corporations and Markets Advisory Committee (CAMAC), an agency that advises on corporations and markets law.
It transfers CAMAC's legal responsibilities to the Commonwealth and the Treasury, and allows the relevant Treasury Portfolio Minister to make rules about these transfers.
The bill also preserves privacy protections for information disclosed to CAMAC and includes transitional arrangements for its cessation.
Repeals Part 9 of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001, which established CAMAC.
Makes consequential amendments to the ASIC Act and provides transitional and savings arrangements for CAMAC's cessation.
Transfers CAMAC's legal responsibilities to the Commonwealth and the Treasury for the operation of Commonwealth laws and the Ombudsman Act 1976.
Allows the relevant Treasury Portfolio Minister (or delegate) to make rules carving out things from the Commonwealth's substitution or prescribing a particular person to take CAMAC's place.
Continues any conditions placed on CAMAC regarding information disclosed under subsection 127(4) of the ASIC Act.
The affected parties are CAMAC, the Commonwealth, the Treasury, and recipients of information disclosed under the ASIC Act.
Statute Update (Smaller Government) Bill 2017 - Third Reading - Pass the bill

The Statute Update (Smaller Government) Bill 2017 was introduced to abolish seven Commonwealth bodies: the Central Trades Committee, Oil Stewardship Advisory Council, Product Stewardship Advisory Group, Advisory Group of the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority, Plant Breeder's Rights Advisory Committee, Development Allowance Authority, and Corporations and Markets Advisory Committee. The government claimed the smaller government agenda had saved an estimated $1.5 billion by the 2016–17 budget and generated $7.6 billion in efficiencies since 2013.

The bill repeals three acts and abolishes seven bodies, including the Corporations and Markets Advisory Committee, which Labor will not oppose because the bodies have already been defunded and de-staffed. Labor argued the abolition reflects the government's disregard for expert advice, citing the Finkel review and drug-testing trials as further examples.

The Statute Update (Smaller Government) Bill 2017 will abolish seven Commonwealth bodies, including the Corporations and Markets Advisory Committee. Labor does not oppose the bill but does not support it, arguing that the smaller government agenda is ideological and that Australia already has a small public sector.
